spots.name: Eiffel Tower approach by Pont d’Iéna
spots.visible_evidence: Facing 180° shows the Eiffel Tower’s lower structure and arch filling much of the frame, with trees at the sides and a crosswalk and traffic in the foreground. This is the strongest direct tower view in the inspected headings.
spots.photo_tip: From a pedestrian area well clear of the roadway, try a vertical frame to emphasize the tower’s height; keep the crosswalk and traffic out of the composition if you want a cleaner architectural shot.
spots.uncertainty: Google Street View imagery is from July 2019. The camera point is geotagged near the road, not a recommended place to stand; use a lawful pedestrian viewpoint and check present-day access. The tower’s visible position suggests this is an approach near its base, but the image alone does not establish a formal viewpoint name.

spots.name: Tree-framed Eiffel Tower view
spots.visible_evidence: Facing 180° shows the tower partly screened by tall trees, with a broad open paved foreground and strong backlighting in this image. The foliage creates a more layered, less direct composition than the other view.
spots.photo_tip: From the pedestrian path, use the trees as a natural frame and shift your position to reveal more or less of the tower. If conditions allow, softer light could reduce the strong glare visible here.
spots.uncertainty: Google Street View imagery is from November 2022; foliage and light are specific to that capture and may differ now. The geotag marks the camera position, not necessarily the best or permitted standing spot. This appears to be an open path or plaza near the tower, but access is not verified.

summary: The clearest tower composition in this small inspected sample is the 180° view at the Pont d’Iéna approach; the nearby 180° view offers a more atmospheric, tree-framed alternative. Other inspected directions were dominated by roadway, vehicles, or street furniture. Images are historical, so they do not establish current access or conditions.
